clue.text: Maybe king seeks romance, giving orders

parts.note: a king is an example of a man, a chess piece
someone who dates is seeking romance

explanation.surface: A king, perhaps, looks for love while issuing commands.
explanation.walkthrough: Chess pieces are called men, so a king is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandates are authoritative commands or instructions, so they are orders.

clue.text: Form are without the greatest teaching aids

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the rearranged letters surround the boxer
to form something is to shape it, so these three letters are rearranged

parts.note: Muhammad Ali called himself The Greatest

explanation.surface: A school form manages without its best teaching materials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form' rearranges the fodder as REA. 'without' is the old sense, outside, not 'lacking'; Muhammad Ali styled himself The Greatest.
explanation.definitionFit: Realia are real objects used in classrooms to illustrate lessons, a kind of teaching material.

clue.text: Slovenly maid to struggle with disapproval

indicators.note: slovenly means messy, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: to vie is to struggle or compete

explanation.surface: A messy maid fights against her employer's displeasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slovenly' rearranges MAID as ADIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a dim view of something is an idiom for disapproving of it.

clue.text: What's left from burning mineral on land

parts.note: ash is the residue after something burns
ore is mineral-bearing rock

explanation.surface: Burnt mineral remains wash up on the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashore describes being on the land rather than at sea.

clue.text: Scientific pioneer drinks behind empty trough

indicators.note: the drinks come behind, so their letters follow the trough's
an empty trough has lost its contents, leaving only the outside letters of the word

parts.note: ales are drinks of beer

explanation.surface: A pioneering scientist sits boozing behind a trough with nothing in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' and 'behind' are the indicators; Thales is often called the first Greek scientist.
explanation.definitionFit: Thales of Miletus is often called the first Greek philosopher-scientist, a pioneer of natural explanation.

clue.text: A specific prohibition for Oedipus?

definitions.note: a person from Thebes, given by example

parts.note: the is the definite article, pointing to a specific thing
a ban is a prohibition

explanation.surface: Asks whether Oedipus was under one particular taboo.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks Oedipus as an example; the taboo hint fits his tragic story.
explanation.definitionFit: Oedipus was king of Thebes, so he is an example of a citizen of that Greek city.

clue.text: Inventive chap not one team rejected

indicators.note: something rejected is thrown back, so these words are read in reverse order

parts.note: not one means no, none at all
a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: An inventor is let down when no team will have him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' signals the reversal; 'not one' means none at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison was the prolific American inventor of the phonograph and a practical light bulb.

clue.text: Pokes head in gallery with unclad figures about

indicators.note: the figures are placed about, around, the gallery's first letter

parts.note: nudes are paintings of unclothed figures

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A gallery visitor peers at naked paintings hung all around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head in' takes G from gallery; 'about' puts NUDES around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nudges are gentle pushes with the elbow, which is what pokes are.

clue.text: Scams to get rich I can see working

indicators.note: letters at work are moved around and put to new use

explanation.surface: Swindles to get wealthy, as I can tell, are working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges RICH I CAN SEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicanery is trickery, so individual chicaneries are deceptions or swindles.

clue.text: Soldiers deal with American going for a whizz in the garden

parts.note: men are soldiers, as opposed to officers

indicators.note: the American abbreviation is going, taken out of the word deal

explanation.surface: Troops strike a bargain with an American who swaps places with a garden expert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going' signals the deletion; the definition is Mendel's pea-breeding in a monastery garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Gregor Mendel founded genetics by breeding peas in his monastery garden, making him a gardening genius.

clue.text: Shelter occupied by masculine, daring explorer

indicators.note: a shelter occupied by something has that thing inside it

parts.note: a hut is a simple shelter
M is the grammatical abbreviation for masculine
bold means daring

explanation.surface: A hut is taken over by a manly, adventurous explorer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occupied by' signals the container: the shelter holds the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander von Humboldt was the Prussian naturalist who explored Latin America at the start of the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Some power revolting leader's half lost

indicators.note: with half its letters lost, only the first half of the leader's name remains

parts.note: Wat Tyler led the Peasants' Revolt of 1381 in England

explanation.surface: A rebel leader loses half his influence.
explanation.walkthrough: Wat Tyler led England's Peasants' Revolt of 1381; 'half lost' leaves the first four of his eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A watt is the SI unit of power, so it is an amount of power.

clue.text: Experimental Greek building structure is broken by old Asian

parts.note: an arch is a structure in a building

indicators.note: the word is is split apart with another piece placed inside it

parts.note: the Medes were an ancient people of Asia, in what is now Iran

explanation.surface: A Greek building's arch is damaged by an ancient Asian invader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken by' splits the clue's 'is'; the Medes were an ancient Iranian people.
explanation.definitionFit: Archimedes of Syracuse was the Greek mathematician famed for experiments such as the bath and displacement.

clue.text: Accounts by modern-style English lawmaker

parts.note: ISA (an Individual Savings Account) and AC (account) are two accounts
new means modern
ton means fashionable style

explanation.surface: An English legislator is backed by fashionable accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: An ISA is a British tax-free Individual Savings Account; TON is old slang for high fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Newton formulated the laws of motion and of gravitation, making him a maker of scientific laws.

clue.text: A lot of odour in dead, decomposing rose

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other, the shortened smell inside the rearranged letters
decomposing things break down, so these letters are jumbled
a lot of a word is most of it, here all but its last letter

parts.note: a scent is an odour

explanation.surface: A strong smell rises from something dead and rotting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decomposing' turns DEAD into A...DED; 'A lot of' cuts SCENT to SCEN, which goes 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose is the past tense of rise, and ascended means went up in the same way.

clue.text: Scientists' device gets them more irritated

indicators.note: irritated letters are agitated and shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Scientists' gadget annoys them all the more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irritated' rearranges THEM MORE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ohmmeter is the instrument used to measure electrical resistance.

clue.text: Material to conceal outmoded hairstyle on top

indicators.note: in a down clue, on top means the hairstyle comes first

parts.note: the DA, or duck's arse, is a 1950s men's hairstyle
to mask is to conceal

explanation.surface: A fabric hides an old-fashioned haircut on someone's head.
explanation.walkthrough: The DA (duck's arse) is a 1950s swept-back men's haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: Damask is a patterned woven fabric, typically silk or linen.

clue.text: An urban space nurtures university intelligence

indicators.note: to nurture is to hold and care for, so the city holds the university

parts.note: a city is an urban area

explanation.surface: A city fosters the brainpower of its university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nurtures' puts U inside A CITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Acuity is sharpness of mind or perception, a form of intelligence.

clue.text: Nobel winner to spoil dog that is repeatedly around

parts.note: to mar something is to spoil it

indicators.note: the repeated abbreviation goes around the dog, which sits between the two copies
repeatedly means the abbreviation appears twice

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A prizewinner is told off for mistreating a dog, again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' doubles the abbreviation and 'around' puts the pair either side of the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Marie Curie won Nobel prizes in both physics and chemistry for her work on radioactivity.

clue.text: Break into rising contented sound during hanky-panky

indicators.note: during means the sound occurs within the hanky-panky

parts.note: it is slang for sex, a form of hanky-panky

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a purr is a contented sound from a cat

explanation.surface: Someone bursts in on a couple purring with pleasure mid-romp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reverses the sound in a down clue, giving RRUP; 'during' puts it inside 'it', slang for sex.
explanation.definitionFit: To irrupt is to burst or force one's way into a place.

clue.text: Woman I am inclined to listen to

indicators.note: listen to says the words are heard, not read

parts.note: I am inclined is I lean

explanation.surface: A woman I am inclined to pay attention to.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'I lean' sounds like the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Eileen is a woman's first name, so it stands for a woman.

clue.text: Measure of speed in walk, not run

indicators.note: not run means the abbreviation for run is removed from the word for walking

parts.note: to march is to walk in step
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Pace is measured as walking, not running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' drops R (run, in cricket scoring) from MARCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mach number expresses speed as a multiple of the speed of sound.

clue.text: Mechanics expert, one kept inside limits

parts.note: a lag, or old lag, is a convict, one kept inside prison
a range is a set of limits, as in the range of a gun

explanation.surface: A mechanic is locked up within certain boundaries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one kept inside' looks like an insertion instruction, but it is a single definition of LAG, a jailbird.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph-Louis Lagrange reformulated classical mechanics, giving his name to Lagrangian mechanics.

clue.text: Pork pie of sizable dimensions for radical pioneer from Germany

parts.note: pork pie is rhyming slang for a lie
something of sizable dimensions is big

explanation.surface: A huge pork pie is offered to a German revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: Pork pie (often 'porky') is Cockney rhyming slang for a lie. 'radical' is chemistry, not politics.
explanation.definitionFit: Justus von Liebig was the German chemist who pioneered the theory of chemical radicals and organic analysis.

clue.text: Stargazer's excited peek left and right

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up, so these four are rearranged

explanation.surface: An astronomer takes an eager glance to left and right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges the glance with left's L, making KEPLE; right's R follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Johannes Kepler was the astronomer who worked out the laws of planetary motion.

clue.text: Cases of horse vaccine seemingly for chemist

indicators.note: the cases of words are their outer letters, the first and last of each

explanation.surface: A chemist seems to supply cases of horse vaccine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cases of' takes HE, VE and SY from the three words.
explanation.definitionFit: George de Hevesy was the Hungarian chemist who won a Nobel prize for radioactive tracers and co-discovered hafnium.
